samples.summary: New document-write entry points (setTaskChecked + the five list commands) carry no readOnly/editable guard, unlike the sibling input handler added in the same change
samples.evidence: `setTaskChecked` (list-commands.ts:294-312) and `toggleBulletList/OrderedList/TaskList`, `indentList`, `outdentList` (255-286) call `view.dispatch({... userEvent: 'input'})` unconditionally — they never consult `view.state.readOnly` or `view.state.facet(EditorView.editable)`. The sibling file added in the same change does exactly that check and documents why (`checkbox-input.ts:22-30`: "A note can be non-writable two ways: the read-only facet, or a non-editable view (what a share-link mount uses)"). Here the only gate is at the mount site: `editor.ts:258` withholds `onToggleTask` when `readOnly`, and `notes-toolbar.tsx:252` (`canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== "view"`) hides the five buttons. That gate is effective at every call site today — I enumerated them: `NotesToolbar` is rendered only from `notes-detail.tsx:198` (member surface, always writable) and `SharedNotesLayout` (`shared-document.tsx:352`) renders `NotesView` with no toolbar at all, and `NoteEditorAPI` is not consumed anywhere else. So this is hardening, not a live bypass. What makes it worth hardening: the write path behind these commands has no second gate either — `note-sync.ts:92` forwards any non-remote `input` transaction to `store.editText` with no readOnly filter, and the server-side backstop defaults off (`yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-88`: enforcement only when `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true'`, otherwise shadow mode returns allow). A future caller that passes `editor` to a toolbar without also passing `readOnly` therefore turns straight into an anonymous viewer-role write, with nothing downstream to stop it. Two lines inside `replacePrefixes` and `setTaskChecked` (`if (view.state.readOnly || !view.state.facet(EditorView.editable)) return;`) would make the guard live in the enforced path instead of at each mount.

samples.summary: The preview's write callback is bound once at mount, so a mid-session role downgrade leaves the new click-to-toggle write path live
samples.evidence: `initialize(container, store, theme, readOnly, ...)` runs in an effect keyed only on `[didMount, doc]` (notes-view.tsx:114-142), and `editor.ts:258` captures the `readOnly` decision into the preview callback at construction time. If `resolved.role` for a share link changes from `editor` to `viewer` after mount (the query in shared-document.tsx re-resolves the link; `readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"` at shared-document.tsx:323 is recomputed on render but never re-mounts the editor), the preview keeps an enabled checkbox whose click still dispatches `setTaskChecked` → `note-sync.ts:96` → `store.editText`. With the Yorkie auth webhook in its default shadow mode (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-88) that write is not rejected server-side either. The same staleness already applies to keyboard editing on this surface, so this change widens an existing window rather than opening one — hence low confidence and minor severity — but it is a new pointer-driven write surface added on top of the stale gate.

finding.summary: New preview click-to-write path is authorized client-side only; the server-side gate it relies on is disabled by default
finding.evidence: This change turns the preview pane into a write surface: `onToggleTask: readOnly ? undefined : (line, checked) => setTaskChecked(view, line + 1, checked)` (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:258-260). The ONLY thing distinguishing a viewer from an editor on this path is the client-side `readOnly` boolean, which comes from `readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"` in packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:323 — a value the browser controls. packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:119-120 asserts the backstop ("a read-only share viewer has no write permission — the auth webhook would reject the update"), and packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:255 repeats it ("A read-only mount passes no callback"). But the enforcement point, packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-105, is gated on `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true'` and defaults to SHADOW mode: when the flag is unset it logs `[shadow] would deny ...` and returns `{ allowed: true }`. `hasAccess` (line 200) is the code that would actually reject a viewer (`needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`) and it is bypassed in shadow mode. Attacker chain: obtain any viewer-role share link, open the note, and issue a Yorkie `rw` update (devtools console against the attached document, or simply patch the client-side `readOnly` value) — the auth webhook returns allow and the edit persists to every collaborator. The write surface added here is new; the missing enforcement is pre-existing, which is why the comments claiming a server-side backstop are the concrete defect to fix (either flip enforcement or stop documenting an inactive gate as the guarantee).

verdict.reason: Every claimed location verified verbatim. editor.ts:253-261 gates the new preview write path (setTaskChecked, list-commands.ts:294) solely on the client-supplied `readOnly` argument; shared-document.tsx:323/352 derives that boolean in the browser from `resolved.role === "viewer"` and attaches a normal realtime DocumentProvider (891-904) with no read-only sync mode. The claimed server backstop (notes-view.tsx:118-120, editor.ts:255) is yorkie-auth.controller.ts, whose enforce flag is `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true'` (86-87) and which returns `{allowed:true, reason:'shadow'}` for every deny when unset (97-105), discarding the only viewer/editor distinction (`needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`, line 200). README.md:111 confirms shadow is the default and no deployment config in the repo sets the flag to true. I found no other server-side check on the Yorkie write path for anonymous share visitors, so a viewer-link holder can persist edits — an authorization weakness inside the Security lane, and the comments asserting an active server gate are the concrete defect.

finding.summary: New list commands and setTaskChecked dispatch document mutations with no readOnly/editable check, unlike the sibling handler added in the same change
finding.evidence: `replacePrefixes` (packages/notes/src/view/list-commands.ts:207-209) and `setTaskChecked` (line 295-300) call `view.dispatch(...)` unconditionally. Neither consults `view.state.readOnly` nor `view.state.facet(EditorView.editable)` — and CodeMirror's `EditorView.editable.of(false)` (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:413), which is what `initialize(..., readOnly)` sets for every share-link mount, only blocks DOM-originated input; it does not block programmatic transactions. The five commands are then re-exported on the public `NoteEditorAPI` (editor.ts:581-585), which `initialize` hands to any host via `onEditorReady`, read-only mounts included. The same change adds `noteCheckboxInput` (packages/notes/src/view/checkbox-input.ts:24-30) which explicitly guards BOTH ways for exactly this reason, so the guard is inconsistent across the write paths introduced together. Today the only host is `NotesToolbar`, rendered solely from notes-detail.tsx:198 (always writable) and never from SharedNotesLayout, so I could not complete an exploit chain — hence low confidence. But `NotesToolbar`'s `readOnly` prop is optional and defaults to falsy (notes-toolbar.tsx:229, 252), so a future read-only host that renders the toolbar gets a fully functional write path on a document it may not write, with the engine offering no enforcement of its own.

verdict.reason: The commands themselves indeed lack an internal readOnly check (list-commands.ts:213, :306), but the readOnly guard the finding says is absent exists at every reachable entry point. setTaskChecked's only production caller is gated: editor.ts:258-260 passes `onToggleTask: undefined` when readOnly, so preview checkboxes are inert. The five list commands' only caller is gated: notes-toolbar.tsx:252 computes `canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== "view"` and line 257 wraps the whole formatting group (list toggles at :300-334) in `{canFormat && editor && ...}`, so they are not rendered on a read-only mount. The read-only share surface never even receives the API: shared-document.tsx:352 renders NotesView with readOnly and no `onEditorReady`, and notes-view.tsx:134 only invokes `onEditorReady?.(editor)` — no host holds NoteEditorAPI there, and no toolbar is rendered. Finally, write authorization is server-enforced, not client-enforced: yorkie-auth.controller.ts:164-200 denies verb 'rw' unless the share link role is 'editor' (the mechanism notes-view.tsx:118-120 explicitly depends on). No DOM, preview, toolbar, or API path reaches these dispatches for an unauthorized actor; the reviewer likewise could not complete an exploit chain. What remains is a defense-in-depth/consistency preference (push the check into the engine for a hypothetical future read-only toolbar host), which is not a blocking access-control defect under the Security rubric.
